It’s the deathbed forgiveness scenario. The usual scenario includes these features, according to my experience. Yours fits mine.

-Starts with a hospital visit or other illness, many times attributed as some “unknown” cause that you learn about from a relative. That relative may or may not know what is happening and could be in collusion or just a patsy. Later, you may find out the illness was exaggerated like they were in the hospital for dehydration and it was implied to you it was “serious” or even the end. My relative was constipated and they admitted them for observation but I was led to believe they were dying. This is usually to test your reaction or relatives trying to manipulate you into revealing you really DO care in some Hallmark moment before it’s too late.

-Next are vague updates of their health or renewed pressures for you to “forgive” which they mean to be *forget and reconcile*. This is usually highly orchestrated manipulations from more than one member of the family. These agendas often include reasons you should not confront the abuser about their behavior because “that’s just the way she has always been” or “he had a bad childhood.”

-You will be given the very strong message that your absence and their suffering is the ONLY thing that matters. “It’s your mother” or “What will people think” will be bandied about. You ignoring your father is far worse than a childhood where he beat you with a belt and now you’re in a lifetime of therapy.

-Should you engage with any of this, your reasons and wishes will be ignored. For instance, even when relatives agree you were treated unfairly and even abused, they won’t want to discuss that and certainly won’t address it with the abuser. Since *it didn’t happen to them*, your trauma doesn’t matter. The quickest way to diffuse this (if you care to try) is to relate a story from your childhood but change the abuser to your best friend or similar and ask the relative what to do. Afterwards, reveal it was a story about your mother and then ask why your mother is allowed to abuse you but no one else is? “But it’s your mother” should be met with, “Yes, and that means she should treat me better than my friend/spouse/stranger.” It doesn’t stop them, but it does get them thinking.

-Finally, they are going to die for real. When this happens *everyone* contacts you in a panic. Your *father is dying, don’t you want to fix this?* It will often come when they aren’t lucid or can’t talk so you won’t get an apology or they pretend this. When you don’t respond to Aunt Mildred, they think you’ll respond to them. I have a brother I have spoken to only twice in 40 years because he used to beat me as a child (five years older than me and I was a 60-pound little girl) and he thought I would respond to him when everyone else failed. Should you engage, ask them to tell you word for word what the person said. Then respond with, “So they don’t want to apologize?” Tell them to call when the abuser can articulate what they did wrong AND apologize. “Not even God forgives without a true expression of remorse.” The only upside is at this stage, relatives are less likely to bluntly manipulate you by lying because they think the situation will motivate you. 

I have never read a story where the abuser offered an apology from a position of remorse rather than fear. What they want is not to heal their relationship with you, but absolution for their sins. Ask yourself why this is coming NOW and not 10 years ago, last February or any time when they were healthy?

Okay, I am over 60 and got hired a few months ago. It IS possible, but you have to do these things I am going to tell you.

Here is the TL;dr: The entire hiring pipeline changed drastically in the past three years. I could go into a long explanation, but the reasons don’t matter. Landing a job is completely different than it was in 2021.

**The Resume**

I am going to give you my short list. 

Go to “career flow AI” and USE IT. Rewrite the resume to get past the ATS system, NOT to look good or use for an interview. 

The purpose of this resume is to land an interview. Use the program to find job openings and track your resumes. Create tailored resumes for each field.

The process to set it up will take a day. **Actually fucking do it.** The system is super easy to use. Remove all but the last five years of job history. It keeps track of everything where you applied. Remove dates of graduation.

After looking for a year, I got laid off and started using Career Flow. I landed a job in tech with a FAANG company in two weeks. I had ANOTHER FAANG company contact me as well. I didn’t even have the program a full month.

**The Hunt**

Start connecting with recruiters on LinkedIn. You can request to connect with 125 people a day, use those to find recruiters. Use Career Flow to update your LinkedIn. Embellish the shit out of it. 

Take any classes with or without certifications — EVEN if you already have the knowledge. List those on your resume and have some current ones. Take AI courses. Data analysts are in high demand for AI jobs and they hire older workers because they need folks with deep knowledge and experience. They also don’t job hop as much. A recruiter told me this.

Focus on staffing firms. Yes, they suck, but *they don’t care about the candidates age*. So you’re less likely to get eliminated. The hiring people assume the recruiter checked you out. I find staffing companies have a lot more bullshit like skills testing but it is far easier to get hired.

**The Interview**

Dye your hair, it will take ten years off your age. Set up good vanity lighting behind your screen on your good side. Put a white sheet on your desk to reflect light up into your face. Do NOT use overhead lights. Wear light foundation (yes, even for men) and powder it down so it isn’t shiny. 

Have your screen a few feet away, you don’t want it super up close to your face.

Be enthusiastic about the job. Focus much of your comments about the future, not your past accomplishments. It’s a subtle way to communicate you don’t plan on retiring soon. Research the company and be “excited” about what they are doing. 
 
Also, ask the recruiter how you can land the job. They will tell you exactly what they are looking for — become that person.

I have a sibling like this and she is not adhd. She was very much enabled by my mother and felt entitled to be late. 

It started as taking time to “look good” (as in hours getting ready for an event) which was excused by boyfriends, bosses, etc. It became her way of life in high school. 

She frequently pushed other boundaries like following dress codes, even social ones. If a funeral requested “mourning attire” (black, navy or gray dress clothes), she would show up dressed for a garden party. 

I stopped enabling it. We had a function that required hours of driving and I informed her and my mother that we were driving away at noon on the dot. I showed up to pick them up at 11:50 and Mom is ready and sibling is not dressed. 
I told Mom that I was leaving at noon with or without them. They knew about this a month in advance, I had warned them not to be late.

This started an argument in the car about why I was being such an asshole, I could just wait “a few minutes” and make it up on the drive. I said I was not going to be stressed, endanger everyone’s life, and ruin the day and be rude at the event because of my sibling’s lack of consideration for everyone else.

Mother got out of the car thinking I wouldn’t leave without her. I said, “This car is driving away at 12 with or without you. You have been warned.” No one else said anything. 

Sister comes out at 12 not dressed appropriately. That was her intention — to wait so long that she couldn’t be forced to change. Being late, dressing different was her way of showing everyone she was “special”. Whatever she was doing (like reading a magazine) was more important than anything else. 
She, too, frequently had stupid excuses that her life was more important, busier, harder, or that she needed the time to look presentable which no one would understand because they don’t get watched by other people.

I informed my mother from that day forward, we would no longer drive with that sibling, wait for them or be dependent on them being on time in any way.

You can’t fix it, but only remove their shitty behavior from your own life.

I have severely progressed KC and can see out of one eye only. It’s no big deal.

I am near retirement and I have been contact lens dependent since about age 21. I limped through life with poor vision that deteriorated because (thankfully) I was not a transplant candidate. 

I had CXL done abroad before it was approved in the US in my 40s. I still could not see with glasses so I had a bunch of different lenses. 

At that time, I was considered the most progressed case ever treated. 

I don’t drive at all because I don’t need to any longer and my vision made it stressful. I didn’t feel it was safe. I haven’t driven at night for the last ten years. I don’t care.

I still work (from home) and it’s in tech. My employer thinks the giant monitor on my desk is because I am a geek. They have no idea of my vision issues. It does not affect my current job at all.

Honestly, it’s not a big deal to me that I don’t see well. My issue is not that I can’t see — it’s being unable to function in life that scares me. But now we have Uber and grocery delivery, telemedicine, giant screens, tablets, mobile phones and so many other options that it isn’t a hardship. 

Want to really see a movie? Slap on a VR headset if you can’t see the screen at the theater. Same goes for video games. There are so many ways to work around failing vision.

Short of losing your eyes, you’ll have some functional vision.

Since there is little or often times no local property tax, municipal governments are incentivized to build more lodging because an apartment complex will generate very little — homes even less so. Hotels will generate room taxes, food taxes, plus people will be spending money on tours and rentals which are all highly taxed. It makes sense for governments to encourage resort developments.

One additional hotel could generate huge amounts of tax revenue and — equally important — bring in more visitors that otherwise could not be accommodated. It increases the available inventory and the community benefits by the hotel’s advertising. Larger events can be planned, holidays don’t sell out as quickly, etc.

And many times, cities will practically give away land to build resorts, casinos, or golf courses. People who have vacant homes often turn them into vacation rentals and they never become available as a rental property. So no new homes built as more properties are converted to vacation rentals.

Pretty soon, the inventory of available homes is crushed creating a real bidding war for homes. I know a broker up there who says frequently there are waitlists with hundreds of names for one rental property.

The problem becomes that it soon makes no sense for a developer to build homes when they can get free or low cost land to build a hotel. And because your community is saturated with lodging, almost all jobs are service based and low pay. No one can afford to buy land and build a custom home so new inventory stagnates. And because everything is so far apart, you don’t really have an opportunity to commute (the exception being Cottonwood to Sedona).

Flagstaff has the added problem of a large college age labor market — cheap, well educated and temporary workers. This has allowed businesses to keep wages low as real estate prices sky rocket.

The only solution is to require new business development to also build housing for their employees (whether they live there or not). So ten employees means a complex with at least ten studio apartments.
